ko.description:

### 맥락

에머슨은 진보하는 영혼이 같은 것을 그대로 되풀이하지 않는다는 주장으로 예술론을 시작한다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

좋아하는 포스터의 색과 배치를 그대로 옮기는 연습에서는 요소가 어떻게 작동하는지 배울 수 있다. 하지만 새 공연을 알리는 포스터라면 관객이 찾아야 할 정보와 공연의 분위기에 맞게 선택을 다시 해야 한다. 이 편집 예시에서 창조는 아무 영향도 받지 않는 일이 아니라 배운 요소를 다른 목적의 전체로 조직하는 일이다. 학습용 모사와 공개할 작품의 출처·권리 문제도 구분해야 한다.

### 읽는 관점

영향받은 것을 그대로 재현하는 대신 어떤 새 전체를 만들지 물을 수 있다.

### 나에게 묻기

지금 만드는 것에서 내 선택으로 바꿀 수 있는 부분은 어디일까?

### 주의할 점

모방 연습은 학습에 유익할 수 있으므로 모든 모사를 무가치하게 볼 필요는 없다.

### 인용 원문

> Thus in our fine arts, not imitation but creation is the aim.

### 출처

English original, 1841; Project Gutenberg \#2944 transcription

en-US.title:
Thus in our fine arts, not imitation but creation is the aim.
— Ralph Waldo Emerson
en-US.description:
**Ralph Waldo Emerson · Essays — First Series · Art**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Emerson begins his account of art with the soul’s effort to make a new whole rather than repeat itself.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Copying a favorite poster’s colors and arrangement as practice can reveal how its parts work. A poster for a different performance, however, needs choices suited to its audience, information and mood. In this editorial example, creation means organizing learned elements into a new purposeful whole, not having no influences. Practice copies also need to be distinguished from work intended for publication, where attribution and rights remain relevant. Originality does not erase those responsibilities.

### A perspective

The line invites a question about what new whole an influence might become.

### Reflect

Where could a choice of your own change what you are making?

### Keep in mind

Imitation can be valuable practice; this need not dismiss every act of copying.

### Source quotation

> Thus in our fine arts, not imitation but creation is the aim.

### Source

[Essays — First Series](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2944/pg2944.txt) · Art

したがって美術における目標は、模倣ではなく創造である。
— ラルフ・ウォルドー・エマソン
ja.description:
**ラルフ・ウォルドー・エマソン · エッセイ第一集 · 芸術**

エマソンは魂が自分を繰り返さず、新しい全体を作ろうとするという考えから芸術論を始める。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

好きなポスターの色や配置を練習として写せば、要素の働きを学べる。別の公演を知らせるなら、観客・必要情報・雰囲気に合わせて選び直す必要がある。この編集例の創造は無影響であることではなく、学んだ要素を新しい目的の全体へ組織することだ。練習用の模写と公開作品も区別し、出典や権利への責任は残る。

### 読みの視点

影響を受けたものから、どんな新しい全体を作るかと問える。

### 自分への問い

今作っているもののどこを、自分の選択で変えられるだろうか。

### 注意点

模倣は有益な練習にもなるため、すべての模写を無価値とする必要はない。

練習臨摹喜愛海報的配色與配置，可看出各部分如何作用；替不同演出做海報，卻須依觀眾、資訊與氣氛重新選擇。這個編輯例子的創造，是把學過的元素組成有新目的的整體，不是完全不受影響。練習仿作也須與公開作品區分，原創性不會消除標示來源與尊重權利的責任。

正在製作的作品中，哪裡能用自己的選擇帶來改變？

模仿可以是有益的練習，不必否定每一種臨摹。

Our thinking is a pious reception.
— Ralph Waldo Emerson
en-US.description:
**Ralph Waldo Emerson · Essays — First Series · Intellect**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Emerson contrasts forcing thought by will with opening the senses and letting intellect see.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

While designing directions, someone may focus only on wording until watching where visitors stop and look around. That observation can suggest a hypothesis about the sign’s location rather than its phrasing. In this editorial example, receptiveness means noticing information outside the answer already favored, not waiting without thought. One observation does not settle the problem; the proposed explanation still needs checking with other visitors and conditions before it guides a redesign.

### A perspective

The passage suggests observing what arrives before pressing an idea forward.

### Reflect

What might you notice if you briefly stopped pushing your current problem?

### Keep in mind

Receiving an intuition does not establish its accuracy or feasibility.

### Source quotation

> Our thinking is a pious reception.

### Source

[Essays — First Series](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2944/pg2944.txt) · Intellect

English original, 1841; Project Gutenberg \#2944 transcription

私たちの思考は、敬虔に受け取ることである。

ja.description:

### 文脈

エマソンは意志で思考を強いることと、感覚を開いて知性に見せることを対比する。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

案内表示の文句だけを考えていた人が、来訪者の立ち止まる場所を観察するとする。すると言葉でなく表示位置が問題だという仮説が生まれうる。この編集例の受容は無思考に待つことではなく、好んでいた答えの外にある情報に気づくことだ。一度の観察で確定せず、別の来訪者や条件でも確かめてから変更につなげる必要がある。

### 読みの視点

考えを押し進める前に、何が現れるかを観察する読み方ができる。

### 自分への問い

今の問題を押し進めるのを少しやめたら、何に気づくだろうか。

### 注意点

直感を受け取るだけでは、正確さや実現可能性の証明にならない。

### 出典の原文

> Our thinking is a pious reception.

### 出典

ko.description:

### 맥락

몽테뉴는 고대 저자의 말을 빌려 자기 생각을 더 잘 표현하는 방식에 관해 설명한다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

— Francis Bacon
en-US.description:
**Francis Bacon · Essays · Of Dispatch**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Bacon criticizes removing necessary parts of business merely to appear quick.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Shortening “If it rains, meet indoors” to “Meet indoors” removes a condition and changes the instruction. “Rain: meet indoors” retains the link between circumstance and action. This editorial example makes meaning, not character count, the test. If a compressed phrase becomes unfamiliar jargon for the reader, expansion may be preferable. A useful reduction preserves the relationships needed to understand when the statement applies while reducing unnecessary reading effort.

### A perspective

In editing, compression can preserve relations that simple deletion would lose.

### Reflect

Which connection must survive in something you are trying to shorten?

### Keep in mind

Brevity need not always be the goal.

### Source quotation

> But it is one thing, to abbreviate by contracting, another by cutting off.

### Source

### 文脈

ベーコンは仕事を早く見せるため、必要な部分を省く態度を批判する。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

「雨なら室内で集まる」を「室内で集まる」に縮めると条件が消え、指示が変わる。「雨天時は室内集合」なら条件と行動の連結が残る。この編集例では文字数より、いつ何が成り立つかが重要になる。短縮が読者に不慣れな専門語を生むなら、説明を戻した方がよいこともある。必要な関係を保ち、余分な読む負担を減らせたかで判断できる。

### 読みの視点

編集でも、関係を保つ圧縮と必要なものを失う削除を区別できる。

### 自分への問い

短くしようとしているものに、必ず残すべきつながりは何だろうか。

### 注意点

短さそのものをいつも目標にする必要はない。

### 出典の原文
